sentences.text: Dollosuchus is an extinct genus containing only one species of tomistomine crocodilian, a group of long-snouted relatives.
This animal possessed large openings above its eyes, a feature also seen in Kentisuchus and Thecachampsa.
The original material used to describe Dollosuchus cannot be distinguished from other related long-snouted crocodilians.
The genus was first described using many jaw fragments discovered in the Early to Middle Eocene Bracklesham Beds Formation in the UK.
A nearly complete skeleton found in Belgium in 1915 was originally described by Swinton in 1937 as Dollosuchus but later became the basis for the separate taxon Dollosuchoides densmorei.
It is no longer likely that Charactosuchus kugleri is a synonym of Dollosuchus because it is now classified in the family Crocodylidae.
Dollosuchus is considered the oldest known tomistomine crocodilian based on recent phylogenetic analyses.
Fossils of Dollosuchus have been discovered in Belgium and the United Kingdom.
Researchers have suggested that Kentisuchus spenceri, Megadontosuchus arduini, and Dollosuchus dixoni might belong to the same genus.
